title: Otter.ai Meeting Transcription and AI Notes
positioning: An AI meeting assistant for recording or importing conversations, producing live transcripts, speaker labels, summaries, action items, searchable meeting history, and workflow-ready meeting knowledge across individual and team use.
decisionAngles: Automatic meeting capture versus bot-free, local, or manually initiated recording workflows
Live transcription and searchable history versus the accuracy review required for names, accents, noise, jargon, and overlapping speech
Cross-meeting AI Chat and workflows versus the risk of treating generated summaries or answers as an authoritative record
Monthly minutes, per-meeting duration, file imports, and conversation-history access versus an apparently simple per-user subscription
Calendar auto-join and automatic sharing convenience versus participant consent, client expectations, and accidental disclosure
Shared team knowledge and integrations versus ownership, retention, archival, deletion, access, and administrator controls
General meeting notes versus sales, enterprise, API, webhook, compliance, and custom workflow requirements

pricingSnapshot.billingUnit: Plans combine per-user access with different monthly transcription allowances, recording or meeting duration limits, file-import allowances, conversation-history access, concurrent meeting capacity, administration, integrations, and enterprise controls.
plans: Basic: free evaluation with monthly transcription, per-conversation, lifetime import, and recent-history limits
Pro: paid individual or small-team tier with higher recording limits, more imports, storage, search, export, and selected integrations
Business: team tier with longer meetings, broader recording and import capacity, concurrent meeting support, and administration
Enterprise: custom security, identity, compliance, API, webhook, sales, and integration capabilities

per-meeting duration, file-import, history, storage, and concurrent-meeting limits

policyBoundaries.label: Recording permission and participant notice remain the user's responsibility
policyBoundaries.summary: Otter can automatically join, record, transcribe, and share meetings, while recording and consent requirements differ by participant, organization, contract, and jurisdiction.
policyBoundaries.releaseGuard: Never imply that calendar access, a host invitation, or the product's recording indicator alone satisfies every legal, workplace, client, or participant-consent requirement.

policyBoundaries.label: Auto-join and auto-share require explicit configuration review
policyBoundaries.summary: Default and event-specific settings can control which meetings the Notetaker joins, whether guests are notified, and who receives or can collaborate on the resulting conversation.
policyBoundaries.releaseGuard: Require users to review global and event-level join, notification, audience, link-sharing, and permission settings before connecting a calendar or using external meetings.

policyBoundaries.label: AI Chat output is not a verified meeting record
policyBoundaries.summary: Otter states that AI Chat can produce incorrect or outdated responses and uses transcript context with internal and external model services when a user asks a question.
policyBoundaries.releaseGuard: Do not present summaries, action items, inferred commitments, or AI Chat answers as exact quotes, professional advice, or verified decisions without checking the transcript and source recording.

policyBoundaries.label: Conversation ownership controls access after plan and workspace changes
policyBoundaries.summary: Downgrades can archive older conversations without deleting them, shared access follows the owner's plan and permissions, and administrators or owners affect access and deletion.
policyBoundaries.releaseGuard: Before organization-wide use, document conversation ownership, export, retention, deletion, offboarding, shared-access, and downgrade procedures.

limitations: Transcription and speaker identification require proofreading when meetings include strong accents, background noise, overlapping speech, uncommon names, or specialized terminology.
Summaries, action items, and AI Chat answers can omit context or be incorrect, so critical commitments and quotations must be checked against the transcript and recording.
Automatic calendar joining can place a bot in internal, client, recruiting, legal, medical, or otherwise sensitive meetings unless global and event-specific settings are reviewed.
Automatic sharing, participant notifications, channels, public links, and collaborator permissions can expose meeting content beyond the intended audience if left misconfigured.
Recording and transcribing other people creates consent, workplace-policy, contractual, privacy, and jurisdiction-specific obligations that the product cannot resolve for the user.
The free tier limits monthly minutes, per-conversation duration, lifetime imports, and accessible history; deleting a conversation does not restore consumed transcription minutes.
Downgrading can archive older conversations and remove shared access based on the conversation owner's plan, even though the data has not been deleted.
Enterprise API, webhook, identity, compliance, and administration requirements may require a custom plan and should not be inferred from the consumer workflow.

Teams should define export, retention, deletion, account offboarding, workspace ownership, model-service, and incident-response procedures before treating meeting history as an organizational knowledge base.

marketValidation.rationale: Otter.ai has substantial independent review volume, long-term product operation, broad meeting-platform integration, and independently covered evolution beyond basic transcription. It has a clear decision role for meeting-heavy individuals and teams. The recommendation remains conditional because accuracy, participant consent, auto-join and sharing defaults, minute and history limits, data governance, and generated-answer reliability can outweigh convenience in sensitive workflows.
strongSignals: G2 listed Otter.ai at 4.4 stars with 504 reviews at review time
TechCrunch independently covered Otter.ai's expansion from meeting transcription into APIs, integrations, MCP access, and enterprise meeting knowledge workflows
Axios previously documented the product's calendar-connected ability to join and transcribe Zoom, Microsoft Teams, or Google Meet meetings with or without the account holder attending
Otter.ai reports more than USD 100 million in annual recurring revenue, more than 35 million users, and more than one billion processed meetings; these scale figures are company-reported
recurringUserFriction: Independent reviews report accuracy drops with accents, noise, jargon, and difficult speaker separation
Automatic joining, participant messages, and automatic summary sharing can surprise teams or external attendees when settings are not reviewed
Plan comparisons require understanding minutes, capture method, duration, imports, history, concurrent meetings, integrations, and administration rather than price alone
Privacy, consent, recording ownership, retention, and deletion become organizational governance questions rather than simple note-taking preferences
